comments: The reference physical geometry is the frozen M166 binary design. Both methods get targets measured from that same geometry in the common FDFD discretization; the geometry coordinates are hidden from optimizer initialization.

This is a method-cost recovery benchmark, not a blind prescribed-pole discovery study. The pre-existing phase-matching period and seed screen are shared preparation and are reported separately from method-specific cost.

Direct controls match complex transmission, not wrapped phase, and may recenter samples using only a counted real-frequency transmittance minimization; they never use a complex-pole location for recentering.

All method-specific objective factorizations, target generation, real-frequency recentering solves, FDFD pole verification, and Fourier H81/H101 validation solves and elapsed time are recorded. The same final physical gates decide success.
No protocol settings may change after scientific run results are seen; an implementation bug fix requires a new run name and a recorded source hash.
